title: Inference value bitecards for platform sellers — iter0
content:
Purpose
---
Short, dense ‘bitecards’ for platform sellers and SEs to use in 1:1s and demo calls. Not a full deck — these are single-slide/one-paragraph artifacts that highlight where Redwood wins and what asks to make. Iterate into final deck after A/B tests with two pilot teams.

Audience
---
- Platform sellers (technical sellers focused on infra/platform teams)
- Solutions engineers running short technical qualification calls

TL;DR (60s)
---
- Problem: Teams struggle to make inference predictable — cost spikes, noisy latency tails, and fragile rollouts across regions/hardware.
- How Redwood helps: unified serving runtime + routing + observability make SLOs achievable without building orchestration.
- Ask: Run a 4-week pilot (hosted -> dedicated bump) with our pilot checklist; target 2-3 key routes for canary.

One-line value cards (use as slide headlines)
---
1) "Costs down, predictability up: 20–40% unit cost reduction on batchy throughput by autoscaling + prefix cache."
2) "Keep the app live on spikes: automatic fallbacks across model tier/region with fewer errors."
3) "Ship faster: same API across hosted/dedicated/private — no rework for prod migration."

60s technical pitch (for SE)
---
- Architecture highlights: GPU-optimized runtime, KV/prefix caching, smart routing policy (latency vs cost), quantized model drops for fallback.
- What to show in demo: 95th latency trace, per-token cost breakdown, route policy config (show config UI), and a live fallback simulation.

Objection response snippets (short)
---
- "We can't trust latency SLAs": show per-route 95/99 latency dashboards + canary rollback demo. Offer a 30-day SLA trial on Dedicated.
- "We already have an internal serving stack": emphasize integration cost vs time-to-stable; present migration estimate (2 sprints) and play up same-API benefit.
- "Cost is lower on our infra": ask for sample traces & token volumes; run quick Optimize analysis (free) to show batching/quantization gains.

Quick tech checklist for qualification call (tick-box to copy into call notes)
---
- Workload shape: avg request length, p50/p95 tokens, burst pattern?
- Primary constraint: latency SLO (ms) or cost target ($/1000 tokens)?
- Data sensitivity: regulated or PCI/PHI? (Private deployment needed?)
- Throughput required (# req/s sustained peak)
- Preferred region & cloud provider
- Existing fallback strategy (if any)

Pilot kickoff play (4-week) — seller asks and SE steps
---
Week 0: Agree scope (2 routes), success metrics (latency p95 < X, cost per 10k tokens), access + sample traffic.
Week 1: Baseline metrics capture (instrumentation + DVR of traces), first Optimize analysis.
Week 2: Config experiments: batching window, cache TTLs, routing policy toggles.
Week 3: Canary run and rollback rehearsals; validate fallbacks.
Week 4: Exec report + ops handoff (CS to own runbook).

Sample battlecard snippets (copyable paragraphs)
---
Enterprise platform architects:
- Pain: heavy governance & long procurement cycles.
- Pitch snippet: "Run without moving sensitive data — our Private control plane + KMS integrations let you keep keys and audit logs. We’ll map your compliance gaps in week 1."

Mid-market SaaS (rapid iteration):
- Pain: unpredictable inference cost as product scales.
- Pitch snippet: "Start hosted, measure unit economics with per-route cost breakdowns, then reserve Dedicated capacity for the top 10% of traffic to cut costs and stabilize latency."

Developer-first startups:
- Pain: want fastest time-to-value.
- Pitch snippet: "Hosted API + model catalog = 10-min demo to product. Use Optimize suggestions to tune for low cost before you scale."

Numbers to call out (place in slide as stat bullets)
---
- Typical outcome: 15–35% token-cost reduction in first month for mixed workloads (prefix caching + batching).
- Median reduction of p95 latency tails after routing & cache = 30% in pilot customers (internal pilot data).
- Time to production for top-proof customers: 2–6 weeks depending on integration complexity.

Handover: SE -> CS (short checklist)
---
- Deliver runbook: canary steps, fallback model mapping, route policies, cost thresholds.
- Share an eval prompt set used for quality gating and any baseline metrics.
- Recommend initial alert thresholds (p95 latency, error rate, cost burn).

Suggested one-slide play templates (for rapid deck assembly)
---
1) "Why Redwood for inference" — one graph (cost vs latency) + 3 bullets (unified API, fallbacks, observability).
2) "Pilot plan & metrics" — scope, 4-week timeline, success metrics.
3) "Quick proof points" — show 3 short wins from previous pilots (anonymized).

Open questions / TODOs
---
- Need anonymized pilot numbers to replace internal stat claims (ask CS for two examples).
- Validate the 15–35% cost reduction claim with latest Optimize runs (ping Dmitri).
- Create slide templates (Leah to mock three single-card slides).
- Run A/B test: hand a subset of sellers these bitecards vs full 6-slide deck; measure conversion to pilot.

Notes to self (voice):
- Keep language concise and prescriptive — sellers want scripts.
- Avoid heavy architecture diagrams in first outreach — use them in follow-up technical sessions.
- Add a tiny ROI calculator snippet (copy/paste) to the final one-pager.
